description: Backend + shared: add a per-game detail capability. Define the GameDetail contract in @mlb/shared, add pure parsers for the MLB linescore + feed/live JSON (and an optional content/recap highlights parser), add MLB client fetchers, extend the DynamoDB store to cache per game under pk=GAME#<gamePk> with a TTL that is LONG for completed games and SHORT for in-progress (Issue #19 acceptance criterion 1), add a BracketService.getGameDetail method with cache-first + upstream-failure fallback contract (criterion 2), and add a GET /game?gamePk= Lambda handler. Fully unit-tested with captured fixtures (no live calls). Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: In shared/src/types.ts add the GameDetail contract types and export them via shared/src/index.ts (it does `export * from './types.js'`). Suggested shapes: `interface InningLine { inning: number; ordinal?: string; away: { runs: number|null; hits: number|null; errors: number|null }; home: { runs: number|null; hits: number|null; errors: number|null } }`; `interface LineScoreTotals { away: { runs: number|null; hits: number|null; errors: number|null }; home: {...} }`; `interface GamePitchers { winner?: string; loser?: string; save?: string }`; `interface GameHighlight { title: string; url: string }`; and the response union: `type GameDetailResponse = { status: 'ok'; gamePk: number; gameState: string; venue?: string; innings: InningLine[]; totals: LineScoreTotals; pitchers: GamePitchers; highlight?: GameHighlight } | { status: 'unavailable'; gamePk: number }`. Document each with JSDoc. The 'unavailable' variant is the documented fallback the frontend uses to keep showing the final score (criterion 2).

Create backend/src/mlb/gameDetail.ts with PURE parser functions and the raw MLB response interfaces (narrowed to consumed fields): `parseLinescore(raw): { innings: InningLine[]; totals: LineScoreTotals }` from the linescore `innings[]` (num, ordinalNum, home/away {runs,hits,errors}) and `teams.{home,away}` totals; `parseGameMeta(rawFeedLive): { gameState: string; venue?: string; pitchers: GamePitchers }` from `gameData.venue.name`, `gameData.status.abstractGameState`, and `liveData.decisions.{winner,loser,save}.fullName`; `parseHighlight(rawContent): GameHighlight | undefined` from `editorial.recap.mlb.{url,headline}` (OPTIONAL - returns undefined when absent, never throws). Keep these side-effect free and defensive (tolerate missing fields, map missing runs/hits/errors to null). Export a helper that assembles a GameDetailResponse 'ok' from the three parsed pieces.

In backend/src/mlb/client.ts add three fetchers mirroring the existing fetchPostseasonSchedule/fetchStandings style (global fetch, throw MlbApiError on non-200, return the narrowed raw type): `fetchGameLinescore(gamePk)` -> raw linescore, `fetchGameFeedLive(gamePk)` -> raw feed/live (use https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1.1/game/{gamePk}/feed/live), and `fetchGameContent(gamePk)` -> raw content (https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/game/{gamePk}/content). The content fetch is best-effort: callers tolerate its failure (highlights are optional per the issue 'if possible').

Extend backend/src/store/dynamo.ts BracketStore interface + DynamoBracketStore with `getCachedGameDetail(gamePk): Promise<GameDetailResponse|undefined>` and `putCachedGameDetail(detail, ttlSeconds): Promise<void>` using a new `gamePartitionKey(gamePk)` -> `GAME#${gamePk}`. Store the detail under a `detail` attribute (mirroring the `bracket`/`winPct` attributes) and keep the existing no-op-when-TABLE_NAME-unset behavior. Add two TTL constants: a LONG TTL for completed games (e.g. GAME_DETAIL_FINAL_TTL_SECONDS = 60*60*24*7, one week) and a SHORT TTL for in-progress (e.g. GAME_DETAIL_LIVE_TTL_SECONDS = 60, one minute). Export the constants so the service can choose by game state.

Add a getGameDetail method to BracketService in backend/src/service/bracketService.ts. Make the new fetchers injectable via BracketServiceDeps (add optional fetchGameLinescore, fetchGameFeedLive, fetchGameContent defaulting to the client functions). Logic: (1) validate gamePk is a positive integer (caller/handler also validates); (2) cache-first via store.getCachedGameDetail - on hit RETURN WITHOUT fetching (criterion 1: cache hit skips fetch); (3) on miss, fetch linescore + feed/live (await both), parse via the pure functions, best-effort fetch+parse content for the optional highlight (wrap in try/catch so a content failure never fails the whole call), assemble the 'ok' GameDetailResponse; (4) write back with TTL chosen by gameState: completed/Final => LONG TTL, else SHORT TTL; (5) on ANY upstream failure (linescore or feed/live throws) RETURN the documented `{ status: 'unavailable', gamePk }` fallback and do NOT throw (criterion 2). Do not cache the 'unavailable' response.

Create backend/src/handlers/getGameDetail.ts following the getBracket.ts handler pattern: `const service = new BracketService(); export const handler: APIGatewayProxyHandlerV2`. Read `event.queryStringParameters?.gamePk`, validate it is a positive integer (reject empty/NaN/<=0 with jsonResponse(400, { message: 'Invalid gamePk; expected a positive integer.' })). On valid input call service.getGameDetail(gamePk) and return jsonResponse(200, result) for BOTH the 'ok' and 'unavailable' variants (the 'unavailable' contract is a 200 so the frontend can gracefully fall back; mirror the prediction handler's union-at-200 approach). Wrap in try/catch returning jsonResponse(500, {message}) only for truly unexpected errors. Add a parseGamePk helper to backend/src/handlers/http.ts (positive-integer parse returning number|undefined).

Export the new handler + service pieces from backend/src/index.ts: `export { handler as getGameDetailHandler } from './handlers/getGameDetail.js';` and re-export the new client fetchers and parsers as appropriate.

Add unit tests: backend/src/mlb/gameDetail.test.ts with CAPTURED fixture JSON (small inline fixtures representing the real linescore/feed-live/content shapes - do NOT fetch live) asserting parseLinescore maps innings + totals (including a null/missing-field case), parseGameMeta extracts venue/gameState/pitchers (and a save-present and save-absent case), and parseHighlight returns the recap link when present and undefined when absent. Add backend/src/service/bracketService.test.ts cases (extend the existing file) for getGameDetail: (a) cache hit returns the cached detail and the fetchers are NOT called (criterion 1 - assert fetch spies not called); (b) cache miss fetches + parses + writes back, and the write-back TTL for a Final game uses the LONG constant while an in-progress game uses the SHORT constant (assert putCachedGameDetail called with the expected ttlSeconds); (c) an upstream linescore/feed-live failure returns `{status:'unavailable',gamePk}` and does NOT throw and does NOT write cache (criterion 2); (d) a content/highlight fetch failure still yields an 'ok' response without a highlight. Add backend/src/handlers/getGameDetail.test.ts following getBracket.test.ts: a missing/invalid gamePk returns 400; a valid gamePk returns 200 with the service result; mock the service or inject a store/fetchers so no live call happens.
Run the backend build + tests to confirm green.
acceptance_criteria: `GameDetailResponse` (ok | unavailable) and supporting types are defined in @mlb/shared and exported.
Pure parsers in backend/src/mlb/gameDetail.ts are covered by unit tests using inline fixtures (no live network).

DynamoBracketStore caches per game under pk=GAME#<gamePk> with a long TTL for completed games and a short TTL for in-progress (criterion 1), proven by a service test asserting the ttlSeconds passed to putCachedGameDetail differs by game state.

BracketService.getGameDetail returns the cached detail on a hit WITHOUT calling the fetchers (criterion 1), and returns `{status:'unavailable',gamePk}` on an upstream failure without throwing (criterion 2).
GET /game?gamePk= handler validates gamePk (400 on invalid) and returns 200 for both ok and unavailable; a content fetch failure still yields an ok response.
findings: Implemented on branch feat/mlb-postseason-site. Commit d63c63b (11 files, +996/-8). Added GameDetailResponse (ok|unavailable) + supporting types (LineScoreSide, InningLine, LineScoreTotals, GamePitchers, GameHighlight) to @mlb/shared/types.ts (exported via index barrel). New backend/src/mlb/gameDetail.ts holds pure, null-tolerant parsers (parseLinescore, parseGameMeta, parseHighlight) + buildGameDetail assembler and the narrowed raw interfaces (RawLinescoreResponse/RawFeedLiveResponse/RawContentResponse). client.ts gained fetchGameLinescore (v1 linescore), fetchGameFeedLive (v1.1 feed/live), fetchGameContent (v1 content) mirroring existing fetchers; the raw types are imported from gameDetail.ts to avoid duplication. DynamoBracketStore extended with get/putCachedGameDetail under pk=GAME#<gamePk> (detail attribute, numeric ttl), plus exported GAME_DETAIL_FINAL_TTL_SECONDS (1 week) and GAME_DETAIL_LIVE_TTL_SECONDS (60s); no-op-when-TABLE_NAME-unset preserved. BracketService got injectable fetchGameLinescore/FeedLive/Content deps and getGameDetail: cache-first (hit returns without fetching), parallel linescore+feed/live fetch on miss, best-effort content highlight wrapped in try/catch, TTL chosen by game state via isCompletedGameState (Final/Game Over/Completed Early => LONG, else SHORT), and {status:'unavailable',gamePk} fallback on any upstream linescore/feed-live failure (not thrown, not cached). New getGameDetail.ts handler (GET /game?gamePk=) with parseGamePk helper added to http.ts (positive-integer, 400 on invalid/missing); returns 200 for both ok and unavailable. index.ts barrel re-exports getGameDetailHandler, the new fetchers, parsers, and TTL constants. Tests: gameDetail.test.ts (9) cover parsers incl. null/missing-field, save-present/absent, highlight present/absent; bracketService.test.ts extended with 5 getGameDetail cases proving cache-hit skips fetchers, Final=>LONG vs in-progress=>SHORT ttlSeconds asserted on putCachedGameDetail, unavailable-on-failure (no throw, no cache), and content-failure-still-ok; getGameDetail.test.ts (3) cover 400 invalid/missing and 200 ok via mocked client. Verification all green with the nvm PATH prefix: `npm run build` (shared->backend->frontend->infra), `npm test -w @mlb/backend` (111 tests, 11 files passing incl. the new suites), and `npm run synth`. No live network in tests (inline captured fixtures + injected mocks).
